title: makemole: building the EPSR-test molecules
purpose: Exercises `makemole`, which converts a molecule template (`.mol`, here of the `.gmol` type) into a single-molecule `.ato` file: it turns the bond lengths and bond angles into the intramolecular distance constraints that EPSR uses to keep molecules flexible but intact, sets up rotational groups and attaches the reference-potential parameters [@epsrmanual]. These single molecules are the building blocks from which `makeato`/`mixato` build the simulation box.
fortran: `ato_manipulation_rev4.f`: `get_rotgrp` (atoms that move with a rotation about a bond), `ftype`
system: The two molecules of EPSR-test. Dimethyl sulphoxide: 10 atoms (S, two C, O, six H) with 9 bonds, 15 angles, the two methyl rotational groups (`rot 1 2`, `rot 1 3`) and Lennard-Jones + charge parameters (S: epsilon 0.84517 kJ/mol, sigma 3.56 Å, q = +0.54 e; O: q = -0.54 e). Water: O1 and two H1 with O-H 0.976 Å and H-O-H 104.5°, SPC/E Lennard-Jones and charges (epsilon 0.65 kJ/mol, sigma 3.166 Å, q(O) = -0.8476 e) [@berendsen1987]. Both files specify 300 K, `vibtemp 65`, `density 0.001` atoms/Å³, so the single molecules sit in cubic boxes of 21.544 Å (DMSO) and 14.422 Å (water).
inputs: `DMSO.mol` and `WaterMolecule.mol` copied from EPSR-test; the second command gives the file name without the `.mol` extension. No standard input is needed because every bond, angle and potential is specified.
verification: One pass of two `makemole` calls; compared files: `DMSO.ato` and `WaterMolecule.ato` (the rewritten `.mol` files come out unchanged). The `.ato` files contain the per-atom constraint lists (e.g. 9 constraints for S) and the rotational groups, so identical files verify the constraint derivation. They differ from the `.ato` files stored in EPSR-test, which were processed further after `makemole`.
